title: Promise scrolls
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 2: The pledges at Aqabah, the Hijrah and zakah
source: Written for islamic-studies/y5 lesson 6 (Pupil PDF worksheet: promise scrolls)
intro: Lesson 6: The pledges at Aqabah and the Ansar. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Visitors from Yathrib
points: Pilgrims came to Makkah each year
The Prophet ﷺ spoke to people from Yathrib
Some believed and took the message home

head: Pledge
Who and when
What they promised
rows: To worship Allah alone, not steal, not slander, obey in good
To protect the Prophet ﷺ as their own families

panels.title: A teacher is sent
points: Mus'ab ibn Umayr went to Yathrib
He taught the Qur'an and Islam
Many homes in Yathrib became Muslim

keywords.def: a pledge: a solemn promise of loyalty
a place near Mina, outside Makkah
the helpers: the Muslims of Madinah

questions.q: Explain why the pledges at Aqabah were a turning point.
questions.a: The people of Yathrib promised to believe and protect the Prophet ﷺ, so the Muslims had a safe home to migrate to.

questions.q: Who was sent to teach in Yathrib?
Write the two pledges as a 'promise scroll' on the pupil PDF: who, when, and three promises, then one sentence on why they mattered.
questions.a: Accurate who and when, promises, and why it mattered

questions.q: Extend: why do you think the people of Yathrib were ready to listen?
questions.a: They wanted peace and guidance; they had heard of a coming prophet; Allah guided them.

questions.q: Stretch: what makes a promise serious in Islam?
questions.a: Allah asks us to keep promises; a pledge is a trust (amanah).

questions.q: What did the second pledge add?
options: A promise to protect the Prophet ﷺ
questions.a: A) A promise to protect the Prophet ﷺ. The second pledge promised protection, preparing for the Hijrah.

questions.q: Think again: why did the people of Yathrib believe?
questions.a: They listened with open hearts and Allah guided them.
